1#_: (1) [Seif 1] Everything that has a permitted aspect, etc. — and even though from the Torah one against two is nullified, as it is written "follow the majority," the Sages were stringent regarding something that has a permitted aspect because there will be permission later — one may not eat it through nullification. Rashi Beitzah 3b. Taz s.k. 1. Peri Chadash letter 1. Levushei Srad letter 1. And see above siman 100 letter 1.
2#_: (2) There. If it was mixed with others, whether whole, etc. — meaning that otherwise it would not be nullified, for it is a counted item and is not nullified, as stated in siman 86; and it teaches here that one should not err to think that a whole egg has only the stringency of a counted item — it teaches that there is also the stringency of something that has a permitted aspect. Taz s.k. 2. Levushei Srad letter 2. And there is a practical difference regarding doubt, as stated below. Taz there. And this is what is written in the next note.
3#_: (3) There. And even if there is doubt whether it was laid on Yom Tov, etc. — in this matter something that has a permitted aspect is stricter than other things that are not nullified, for there we are lenient in their doubts if the prohibition is certainly d'rabbanan — we say in his doubt it is permitted like any d'rabbanan doubt, and it will not harm him if it is an important item; but here, even in a d'rabbanan prohibition doubt, it is forbidden since it has a permitted aspect. Taz s.k. 3. And so Peri Chadash letter 2 — something that has a permitted aspect, even in a d'rabbanan doubt, and even in a thousand is not nullified, since there is permission for its prohibition. Levushei Srad letter 4. Chokhmat Adam general rule 53 letter 19. And so is the opinion of the Shulchan Aruch in what it wrote: "and even if there is doubt whether it was laid on Yom Tov," which is a d'rabbanan doubt, and it was mixed with forbidden eggs. However, see in our words in Orach Chayim siman 513 letter 6, where we wrote that there is permission in a d'rabbanan doubt mixed with others, only that we wrote there to be stringent like the Shulchan Aruch and its reasoning, only for great need or great loss one may rely on the permission — see there.
4#_: (4) There. And it was mixed with other forbidden items. And if from those mixtures it was mixed again with others — see below siman 110 seif 8 in the hagahah.
